changes.balance: Friday's −2% de-escalation fade is the reversal risk — the premium re-embeds on the reopen.
changes.body: The offer (via Qatar at UNGA): cease hostilities, reopen Hormuz within seven days, restart nuclear talks — in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, releasing ~$12B in frozen assets, easing oil-export sanctions. Trump Saturday: 'They made a proposal, but I rejected it' — 'they're losing so badly.' Wall Street Journal: privately skeptical of any ceasefire; expects US bombing to resume after the November midterms. Sunday: FM Araghchi says Iran won't soften conditions; the US naval blockade stays 'in full force.'
changes.title: Trump rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz plan

changes.balance: ~13.5 MMb/d clearing the strait — near the July ceasefire peak — but the paper-vs-physical wedge (VLCC $1M+/day, Hormuz→Asia freight >$22/bbl) keeps the flat-price premium embedded.
changes.body: Tanker Trackers: Persian Gulf oil volumes have doubled in under a month as US forces now escort daytime transits (mines cleared from the main corridor). Kpler via Reuters: ~18 transits/day 10-day average; 33.7 MMbbl flowed out in the week starting Sep 20, roughly on par with the prior week. Javier Blas (Bloomberg Opinion): hiring a very large crude carrier runs $1M+/day, freight from inside Hormuz to Asia exceeds $22/bbl vs ~$2 a year ago.
changes.source: Tanker Trackers / Commodity Context / Javier Blas
changes.title: Gulf tanker volumes doubled in under a month

changes.balance: Catch-up risk: WTI length is the lagging overhang — fresh escalation squeezes WTI hardest off the $11.91 spread.
changes.body: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) managed-money futures-only net long +101,828 (−4,451 w/w) — ~96th percentile of its 56-week range: crowded long by historical standards. Brent managed money (futures+options) net long +218,114 (−64,543 w/w) — specs cut ~23% of length in one week; the Brent crowded trade just washed.
changes.delta: WTI length at 96th percentile; Brent specs −23% in a week
changes.title: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent washed
changes.vintage: Data as of Tue Sep 22, released Fri Sep 25

changes.balance: ~275 kb/d of WCS demand still offline — the diff stays pressured until full rates.
changes.body: Several units at the ~275 kb/d Illinois refinery returned Wednesday (Quantum Commodity Intelligence, Sep 24) — but Exxon has issued no public restart date and no confirmation of normal service. Offline = Western Canadian Select (WCS) wider and weaker; a confirmed full restart = the snap tighter for Nov/Dec.
changes.title: Joliet partial restart only

changes.balance: ~300 kb/d of synthetic supply offline plus record distillate cracks — doubly supportive for SCO/WCS relative value.
changes.body: Back ~mid-October (~day 20 of 35). Horizon essentially fully offline — roughly 300 kb/d of synthetic crude out. Second leg: the gasoil crack vs Brent printed a record ~$95/bbl (data back to 2011); NY Harbor ULSD crack ~$97 Friday after a record $113.48 Sep 16. Distillate-rich synthetic crude is the prime beneficiary. Cumulative Russian diesel destruction (Perm halted, Ilsky hit, Novoshakhtinsk suspended) adds more fuel.
changes.delta: ~300 kb/d SCO offline; gasoil crack record ~$95/bbl
changes.source: Heavy Reading maintenance calendar / ICE / RBN Energy
changes.title: Horizon ~day 20 of 35; record distillate cracks

changes.balance: Spare takeaway −38 kb/d m/m against record Q4 supply — widening-risk bias into winter.
changes.body: Carry-forward June 2026 data: Keystone ~94%, Trans Mountain ~96%, Enbridge Mainline ~94% of available capacity. Spare takeaway down from ~310 kb/d in May. Oil Sands Magazine (Sep 22) puts Q4 basin production at a record 4.8 MMb/d. The Mainline is back into apportionment for October: light 8%, heavy 4% at Kerrobert (official Enbridge notice, Sep 16; Line 1: FPA 7% Regina, SPA 3% Kerrobert).
changes.title: Egress functionally full; Mainline apportioned for October

changes.balance: While Jose→USGC freight holds at ~$7/bbl, Merey prices down to clear against WCS at Houston cokers — direct WCS widening pressure.
changes.body: Merey discounts deepened to −$18/−$20 under Brent (Sep 26 report, small outlet, unverified) vs −$14 to ICE Brent for October cargoes (Bloomberg, Sep 24). The widening is freight-driven — Aframax Jose→USGC $1.35M → $3.5M with war clauses — not demand-driven, so it could snap back if vessel availability improves.
changes.title: Merey discounts deepen on war-risk freight

changes.balance: WTI lost 7.9% on the week; Brent held the Hormuz premium. Framing per standing rule: this is the global balance, not Cushing.
changes.body: Friday settles: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Nov26 $92.41 (−2.33%), Brent Nov26 $104.32 (−2.14%). WTI-specific drags: the surprise +2.969 MMbbl EIA build (vs ~0.64 draw expected), the November contract roll, and diesel-export-ban chatter pressuring US refiners' margins. Curve in steep backwardation — tight now, relief later.
changes.title: Brent–WTI blows out to 2026 wide

flags.body: Trump endorsed a diesel export ban Sep 22 with a fast decision promised; current posture is voluntary refiner export cuts (no federal ban ordered). A ban traps barrels at home and crushes the record cracks supporting synthetic crude.
